title: Fermionic Gaussian Scrooge Ensembles in Deep Thermalization
abstract: Measuring part of a many-body wave function generates a projected ensemble of pure quantum states on the unmeasured subsystem. Recent advances in deep thermalization have shown that, in chaotic systems, this ensemble universally converges to the maximally random ensemble compatible with its average density matrix, known as the Scrooge ensemble. By contrast, free-fermion systems are nonchaotic, and their quantum states are constrained to remain Gaussian. Motivated by this distinction, we introduce the fermionic Gaussian Scrooge ensemble to describe deep thermalization in generic free-fermion systems. This ensemble is defined as a distortion of the Gaussian Haar ensemble by the average density matrix, and its moments reveal an enlarged symmetry of Gaussian states in the replicated Hilbert space. We demonstrate the emergence of the fermionic Gaussian Scrooge ensemble in two complementary settings: (1) we analytically prove that the projected ensemble of the SYK$_2$ model follows the fermionic Gaussian Scrooge ensemble at arbitrary evolution times; (2) we provide numerical evidence that it emerges at sufficiently long times in random Gaussian circuits with charge conservation. Our results establish the fermionic Gaussian Scrooge ensemble as a universal description of deep thermalization in free-fermion systems.
summary: This work introduces the fermionic Gaussian Scrooge (fGS) ensemble to universally describe deep thermalization in free-fermion quantum systems. By analyzing the projected state after measurement, the authors prove that the ensemble converges to this specific Gaussian distortion, validating it for models like SYK2 and random Gaussian circuits. This provides a crucial theoretical tool for understanding quantum information scrambling in non-interacting fermionic settings.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical description of deep thermalization in free-fermion systems following partial quantum measurements.
main_result: It establishes the fermionic Gaussian Scrooge (fGS) ensemble as the universal description for this process, proving its emergence for models like SYK2 and random Gaussian circuits.
method: The authors use the replica trick and path integral methods, combined with a canonical purification technique, to calculate the moments of the projected quantum state ensemble.
model_or_system: The study focuses on free-fermion systems, exemplified by the SYK2 model and random Gaussian circuits, where the evolution is governed by quadratic Hamiltonians.
key_observables: The projected ensemble moments ($ho_{PE}^{(k)}$), the correlation matrix ($\Gamma$), and the deviation from the fGS ensemble ($\Delta f_{GS}(k)$).
important_parameters: Evolution time ($t$), system size ($N$), and parameters defining the initial state (e.g., $p$ and $	heta$ for Gaussian circuits).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the system remaining Gaussian throughout evolution and utilizes the large-N expansion and saddle-point approximation for path integrals.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic construction of the fGS ensemble, the path integrals and saddle-point solutions for SYK2, and numerical convergence plots showing the measured ensemble approaching the fGS prediction.
paper_structure: The paper develops the fGS ensemble definition via purification, applies the replica trick to calculate projected moments for SYK2, and then confirms this universality numerically using random Gaussian circuits.
why_interesting: The concept of a universal ensemble describing thermalization in non-chaotic (free-fermion) systems provides a powerful, analytically tractable generalization of concepts from chaotic systems.

FIG. 1. Numerical results for random Gaussian circuits with U(1) symmetry. In all panels, we set NA = 4 and NB = 300 and sample Ns = 105 measurement outcomes. The results are obtained from a single realization of both the initial state and the random circuit. The shaded regions indicate the statistical uncertainty due to Monte Carlo sampling. The results clearly demonstrate convergence to the fGS ensemble with a nontrivial average density matrix for p < 1.
